# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** housekeeper and housemother  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Titles:** queen of housemothers  <sub>[v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with a small, softly-triangular face and large, soft blue eyes filled with unquenchable youth. She has pink cheeks and wears her snow-white hair in quaint little puffs over her ears. She dresses in an old-fashioned style.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina describes herself as old-fashioned in her clothes and opinions, preferring comfortable ways over modern ones. She possesses a youthful mirthfulness, charm, and a twinkling sense of humor, often making fun of her beaux in her youth and expressing her mind frankly. Though loving, she holds a low opinion of Phil Gordon's antics because she cannot fully understand her. She detests visiting and holds a deep respect for the clergy.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c18 P2](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0002), [v3 c19 P40](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0040), [v3 c20 P10](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0010), [v3 c24 P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005), [v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021), [v3 c37 P42](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0042)_

## History

Aunt Jamesina was born a month after her father James drowned at sea. She grew up longing for a yellow silk dress, but neither her mother nor her husband permitted her to buy one. She eventually raised a daughter, Elizabeth, who previously wrote stories before marrying and leaving for the foreign mission field in India. Left alone in a large house, Aunt Jamesina moved to Patty's Place in Kingsport to keep house for Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Phil Gordon, and Stella Maynard. She cared for the household and three cats—Rusty, Joseph, and the Sarah-cat—while remaining worried about her daughter facing snakes in India.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)_

## Background by volume

- named Jamesina after her father James who drowned at sea a month before her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- never attended college  <sub>[v3 c37 P14](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0014)</sub>
- always wanted a yellow silk dress, but her mother and husband forbade it  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- suggested to a suitor in her youth that he train his sticking-out ears with a rubber band  <sub>[v3 c37 P40](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0040)</sub>
- laughed at her suitors when she was young  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>
- prayed that her daughter would become a missionary  <sub>[v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>

## Quotes

> It’s a very old-fashioned way. But I am old-fashioned. My clothes are, and it stands to reason my opinions are, too.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> The weather has been real cold, so I let the cats sleep in the house—Rusty and Joseph on the sofa in the living-room, and the Sarah-cat on the foot of my bed.  <sub>[v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025)</sub>

> The very first thing I’m going to do when I get to heaven is to get a yellow silk dress.  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

> It isn’t in good taste to make fun of your beaux; but I always did it myself.  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>

> You’ve been to college four years and I never was, but I know heaps more than you do, young ladies.  <sub>[v3 c37 P14](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0014)</sub>
